acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one dated vault source with tracked visibility naming the document appears in that project's vault map and is queued for distillation; a failed or empty firing adds none
acceptance_criteria.when: a retrospective is written

acceptance_criteria.given: the job on with a runner whose spawn fails
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test with a failing worker
acceptance_criteria.then: both succeed with no added delay waiting on the job, and a manager_job_fired event with outcome failed is recorded
acceptance_criteria.when: the last task is approved and the document is then archived

acceptance_criteria.given: a build with one run per flag (send-back, stall, failed, mender, over twice the median) and three ordinary runs
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test on the input builder
acceptance_criteria.then: all five flagged runs' transcripts are included, no ordinary run's transcript is, and the report lists exactly the five
acceptance_criteria.when: the input is assembled

acceptance_criteria.given: a seeded four-task build whose input is larger than the model's limit (a test limit set low) but each task's records fit, and a second build that fits
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test with a stubbed worker recording its inputs
acceptance_criteria.then: the first makes more than one part call, no task's records appear in two parts, then one final call whose input holds the part reviews, and its report states the number of parts; the second makes exactly one call
acceptance_criteria.when: each is reviewed with a stubbed worker

acceptance_criteria.given: two task check runs and one landing-batch run queued while two other runs hold both slots
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub tests at the slot-acquire seams in project_checks.py and landing_queue.py; fail on master (no column)
acceptance_criteria.then: each run's stored row has a slot time later than its started_at, including the landing-batch run, and a run cancelled while waiting has none
acceptance_criteria.when: slots free and the waiting runs start their checks, and the modules' in-memory state is then cleared as a restart would

acceptance_criteria.given: a build whose three tasks build in parallel for 1 h while their check runs total 2 h, one of which timed out, with rows in the order the tally's queries return them
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test through the build figures route, modelled on AWOAW 2026-11-05
acceptance_criteria.then: check running plus waiting totals 2 h, the timed-out count is 1 and that run is not in failed, and the wall bar's parts still sum to the build's wall time. On master the route gives no running/waiting/timed-out figures
acceptance_criteria.when: the build card's figures are read through the route the spec page calls

acceptance_criteria.given: a build whose check runs have no slot time, and one mixing old and new runs
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test through the same route
acceptance_criteria.then: the first reports waiting as null with its runs counted as running; the second reports the new runs' waiting and the count of runs with no slot time
acceptance_criteria.when: its figures are read

acceptance_criteria.given: a build with one task approved at 11:40 and landed at 16:58, one landed within 10 min, and one approved and not yet landed
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: hub test through the same route
acceptance_criteria.then: longest landed wait is 5 h 18 m, the total is their sum, and one task is reported still waiting with its wait so far
acceptance_criteria.when: its figures are read

acceptance_criteria.given: the build figures from the AWOAW-shaped fixture, and one with unknown waiting
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: vitest on SpecBuilds with the route's payload
acceptance_criteria.then: the Checks meter shows running and waiting with a 2 h total, the timed-out count and the landing wait appear, and the unknown waiting reads as unknown
acceptance_criteria.when: the spec page's build card renders

acceptance_criteria.given: a fresh build on the trial Hub :8010 with two tasks whose checks run while both are still building
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: scripts/drive drive written first and failing on master
acceptance_criteria.then: the card's Checks total equals the sum of the build's check-run durations read from the check-run route, and the landing wait is shown
acceptance_criteria.when: both tasks are approved and land

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: how a spec is built is chosen when building starts, not inside the spec; the record is what slices F and G read.
requirements.statement: Starting a build of an approved document records a build with its driver (flow, lead or hand), level (fast, reviewed or gated), builders, reviewer pool, lead, budget cap, window and landing, readable afterwards from the document; Build and 'Approve and build' open with the recommended build filled in; a second build of the same document is refused while one is running, naming it.

requirements.rationale: 'Every task records the level it was built under' (roadmap); a null level keeps every flow and task created before this change behaving as it does now.
requirements.statement: Every task a build covers records that build and its level when the build starts (or when it joins a running build), and every transition of that task records the level that governed it; a task outside any build records none and is governed exactly as today.

requirements.rationale: F1046. Kept rather than refused for the reason `reviewer` is (spec_payload.py:164-167): an author cannot know which agents the running machine has. Applied at build start, not approval, because slice C makes approval a plan.
requirements.statement: A spec task may declare a builder by agent name; when a build starts, a declared builder that is an open agent becomes the task's assignee unless the operator changed it in the Build dialog, and one that is not is kept on the task, reported in the start's response, and the task left for the driver to hand out.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-27: T3 went to the Architect (Opus) only because it was free.
requirements.statement: A flow-driven build hands fresh work only to its builders and staffs reviews only from its reviewer pool (each list, when empty, meaning any free agent as today); a task's own declared builder or reviewer still takes precedence; no other agent is given a turn on the build's tasks.

requirements.rationale: The lead exercises the judgement the 2026-10-25 retrospective found missing in the middle; its authority is scoped to one build (roadmap non-goal: no project-wide god agent).
requirements.statement: A lead-driven build gives its lead a turn when it starts and whenever one of its tasks is completed, sent back, approved or rejected, without stacking a second brief on an unread one; the lead hands a task to one of the build's builders, or a review to one of its reviewer pool, with a tool answered only for the lead of that task's running build; a hand-driven build starts no turn at all.

requirements.rationale: Slice B's non-goal names Fast as where author-may-not-approve becomes a choice; slice B's resolved question says already-built tasks close at once at Fast.
requirements.statement: At Fast, a completed task is approved without a reviewer turn: by its builder or its build's lead directly from completed, or, in a flow-driven build, by the flow once the task's check run has passed; and closing a document's tasks as already built (slice B) at Fast approves them at once.

At Reviewed, any agent other than the task's builder (the lead included) or the operator approves it, and requirements the task serves that lack accepted evidence are reported in the approval's response, never refused.
At Gated, the builder cannot approve, and approval is refused until every requirement the task serves has evidence accepted, as a `gate`-rigor document's tasks are today.

requirements.rationale: The night of 2026-10-26/27 cost ~$44 with nothing to stop it; turn_usage carries api_equivalent_usd_micros on 428 of 436 turns on :8000 (read-only query, 2026-10-27).
requirements.statement: A flow- or lead-driven build hands out no new turn before its window opens, after it closes, or once the API-equivalent cost of its runs reaches its cap; turns already running finish; reaching the cap stops the build with the spend and the cap in its reason and notifies the operator, and raising the cap or extending the window resumes it.

A build lands its approved work on the project's main branch as today, or nowhere: a task of a build that lands nowhere is approved with nothing merged and its integration record says the build lands nowhere.

requirements.rationale: Slice B's invariant, extended: levels and a lead are new inputs to its one decision, and must not add a dead end.
requirements.statement: For every level, every non-terminal status and every holder (none, the builder, another agent, the mender, the build's lead), at least one actor can move the task on with the tools it is offered, blocked excepted (its mover is the operator).

requirements.rationale: Naming people only where they differ from the default is why the split reaches the operator undone.
requirements.statement: An author writing a change document is asked to name a builder and a checker on every task, chosen from the open agents, each with a one-sentence reason.

The author is told each open agent's model, and each reason states the pick in terms of that model's cost and performance and the task's complexity, and nothing else. Within one document, a hazardous task and a routine task can receive different agents.

requirements.rationale: A search or review costs quota, and the operator knows whether the author's view is current.
requirements.statement: Before naming people on a document larger than a fix, the author states its current view of the roster's models and asks the operator which sources to use, in any combination: what it already knows, a web search, or a review of this project's record. It uses only those chosen, and records what it found in the document's evidence. If a chosen source is unavailable, it says so rather than presenting a guess as the finding.

requirements.rationale: The review needs figures an agent cannot otherwise reach. An agent's model can change, so attributing by agent would credit the wrong model.
requirements.statement: Any agent can read this project's record per model: tasks built, send-backs by reason class, and API-equivalent cost, each with its sample size. A task counts under the model that actually ran its build turns, and unpriced turns are reported as unpriced, not counted as zero.

requirements.rationale: A builder cannot check their own work at the Reviewed level, so such a pick could never be carried out.
requirements.statement: A task's recommended checker is never its recommended builder. When a project has one open agent, the checker is left empty and the reason says why.
Build opens with each task's recommended builder and checker selected and its reasons visible beside that task's row. The operator can change any of them, and the choice made is what is built.

requirements.rationale: Approvals are scarce: warn, do not gate (operator, 2026-10-08).
requirements.statement: A task with no recommended builder or checker, or a pick with no reason, draws a warning on the document naming the task, and never blocks approval.
When a recommended agent is no longer open at Build, the dialog says so on that task's row and does not select them. Documents with no recommendations open Build as they do today.
A task filed against a spec whose build is running goes to that build's default builder and is checked by its default checker, unless the task names its own.

A task filed against a spec whose latest build finished by running out of work reopens that build, however long ago it finished, at the same level, landing and budget cap, and takes its people as a running build's follow-up does. The build record shows that it reopened, and the spec stops reading as done until the task has landed.

requirements.rationale: The operator chose to manage unwanted restarts themselves (2026-11-01), which works only if they learn of a restart while they can still stop it.
requirements.statement: Every reopening shows the operator a warning on the Overview screen, naming the spec, the task, who filed it, and how long ago the build had finished, with a way to stop the build from the warning. The warning stays until the operator dismisses it or the build ends.

In a flow-driven build, a follow-up is started by a flow within two firings of being filed, including when the build's earlier flow had already stopped on an empty queue, with no operator or agent action. A hand-driven build's follow-up waits on the board under its builder for the operator to start.

requirements.rationale: A stop is a decision; a finish is only the absence of work. Reopening a stopped build would spend what someone chose to stop spending.
requirements.statement: A follow-up filed against a spec whose latest build was stopped, whether by the operator, its budget cap or its window, or against an archived spec, restarts nothing and shows no reopening warning. It stays on the board with no build, the filer is told why, and on a non-archived spec the operator's next Build takes it in.
Two follow-ups filed together reopen one build and one flow and show one warning naming both, and a second driver on the reopened build is refused as on any running build.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: one person checks it. Having two roles that each judge the work is what left the dialog with fields nobody filled.
requirements.statement: A change document names, for each task, at most one builder and at most one checker, plus a build-wide default builder and default checker; the checker of a task is the single agent who both tests it and records its verdict.

requirements.rationale: Approved documents are not reopened just to rename a field, and a build of one must not lose its reviewer. The tester wins because the single checker drives the product (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: A document saved before this change that names `reviewer`, `tester` or a task's own `reviewer` builds with those agents as its checkers, without the document being edited. A task's own reviewer is that task's checker; otherwise the tester, if named, is the default checker, else the reviewer.

The Build dialog opens with every person the document names already selected: the default builder, the default checker, and each task's builder and checker. No person the document names is shown only as text, or left out.

Starting a build writes the operator's choices into the spec document: the driver, the level, the default builder and checker, each task's builder and checker, the lead, the budget cap, the window and the landing. They sit beside the author's recommendation, labelled as the operator's, and the recommendation is left unchanged.

`read_spec_document` returns the document's running build, with every choice listed in choices-in-the-spec, marked as the operator's choice and kept apart from `delivery`. A turn started to work on or check one of the build's tasks names the build's driver and that task's builder and checker.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: the last ended build explains the latest change of plan; a full history would grow the tracked file on every restart.
requirements.statement: When a build stops or finishes, the spec document shows that build as ended, stopped or finished, with when, and `read_spec_document` no longer reports it as running. The document holds at most the running build and the most recent ended build; an older ended build leaves the document and stays on the build record.

requirements.rationale: F1083: a second driver re-pointed a hand build's tasks at a flow the operator never chose.
requirements.statement: Creating a flow or a loop for a document whose build is running is refused with 409, and the refusal names the build and its driver. No task's flow or loop changes as a result. Starting a build that is driven by a flow still creates that flow.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: hold rather than hand to someone else, so a broken plan shows instead of being quietly substituted.
requirements.statement: In a flow-driven build, a task whose builder is an open agent is worked only by that agent, whether or not the agent is in the build-wide builders list or is named as a checker elsewhere. While that builder is busy, the task waits for them and is not given to anyone else. A task whose builder is not an open agent is held, given to nobody, and says on the task that its builder is not an open agent.

In a flow- or lead-driven build at Reviewed or Gated, a finished task's check goes to that task's checker, or to the default checker when the task names none, and never to the agent that built it. A checker that is not an open agent holds the check and says so on the task, rather than passing the check to someone else. At Fast no check is handed out.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: by hand is for me to start it, and I send the check myself. Pending rather than Assigned, because a move to Assigned starts the agent today.
requirements.statement: In a hand-driven build, every task whose builder is an open agent shows on the board in Pending with that agent named as its builder, and its checker named. No run is started and no message or queued input reaches any agent until the operator asks one to pick up a task or a check.
In a lead-driven build, the lead's brief names each task's builder and checker, and a task the lead hands to anyone other than its named builder is recorded with who it went to.

requirements.rationale: The build plan is one plan: the operator reads and changes it in one place, task by task, as the agents will be given it.
requirements.statement: Build and Approve and build on a change document MUST open one dialog with two sections: 'How it runs' (who hands out the work, the level, the lead when the driver is a lead, the flow's stop rule and schedule in words when it is a flow, where the work lands, the budget cap, and when the build stops handing out work) and 'Who builds and checks' (the default builder, the default checker, and one row per declared task, in the document's order and by its title, with that task's builder and checker).

requirements.rationale: The operator decides; the recommendation and its reason are what they decide from, and a missing reason is a gap in the spec they should see.
requirements.statement: Every choice in the dialog MUST open on the document's recommendation, with the reason the document gives for it shown beside the control; a task's builder or checker that is recommended without a reason MUST read 'No reason given', and one with no recommendation MUST read 'No recommendation'.

A task's builder or checker changed from its recommendation MUST name the recommended agent and offer to put it back, and the dialog MUST say how many tasks differ from the recommendation, or that the plan is as the document recommends.

requirements.rationale: What is shown is what is sent: a closed agent selected silently would be sent and refused, or worse, sent and stall.
requirements.statement: A recommended agent that is not an open agent of the project MUST NOT be selected; its row MUST say that the recommended agent is not open, and the task falls to the default.

requirements.rationale: The Hub refuses a task whose builder would be its checker; the dialog says so before the operator presses Build, on the row that causes it.
requirements.statement: At the Reviewed and Gated levels, a task whose builder (its own, else the default) is also its checker (its own, else the default) MUST be marked in its row, and the dialog MUST NOT confirm until no task is.

requirements.rationale: The build the Hub records is the operator's decision (a-build-has-a-driver-a-level-and-its-people); the dialog must not add or drop a choice between screen and record.
requirements.statement: Confirming MUST send exactly what the dialog shows: driver, level, landing, default builder and checker, each task's builder and checker (empty where it falls to the default), the lead for a lead, the cap when one is given, the window end chosen, and as builders the distinct agents that build some task. The flow's agent MUST be sent only when the default builder differs from the recommended flow agent.
At the Fast level the dialog MUST NOT show the default checker or any task's checker, and MUST NOT send checkers.

requirements.rationale: The mock rules (hub/ui/mock/README.md, rules 2 and 5); today's dialog breaks both.
requirements.statement: Every agent the dialog lists MUST carry its colour as the rest of the app shows it and, where the Hub reports one, its model; the dialog MUST use the app's themed controls only, with no native select, checkbox or date input.
The dialog the app ships MUST match the mock the operator approved on 2026-11-03, in dark and in light.

requirements.rationale: Every model the Hub spawns on its own is the operator's to switch on and pay for; the manager registry is where that choice lives today (hub/hub/manager.py JOBS).
requirements.statement: The Manager page lists a 'Build retrospective' job that the operator can turn on or off and give a runner and a model per project, like the other manager jobs; it needs a runner, and with no row or turned off it never fires automatically.

requirements.rationale: The Hub already detects this moment for the chapters job (chapters_job.py LAST_TASK_APPROVED); a build that finished is the one whose lessons are cheapest to miss.
requirements.statement: While the job is on with automatic firing, approving the last open task of a spec document in any project fires exactly one retrospective of that document's build.

requirements.rationale: The builds most worth reviewing are often the ones that stalled and never finished, like the 2026-10-25 flow.
requirements.statement: A 'Review this build' action on a spec document's page fires a retrospective of that document's build whenever the job has a runner, whether or not every task is approved and whatever the automatic choice; while one is running for that document a second request starts nothing and says one is in progress.

A retrospective's input holds, for every task of the document: its status transitions with who and when, its runs with agent, model, duration, outcome and cost, its notes, its evidence and every decision on it, its check-gate runs and results, the stalls and mender interventions naming it, the checkpoint summaries of its runs, and the document's amendments, reconcile gaps and the ask_user questions raised in its runs with how long each waited for an answer.

requirements.rationale: A model's arithmetic over dozens of runs is a guess, and in a build reviewed in parts no single call sees every run.
requirements.statement: Every time and cost figure in the report (per task: time building, waiting for review, in the check gate, and waiting to be started; per agent and per task: cost and tokens; build totals) is computed by the Hub from the records, not estimated by the model, and equals what the records give.

The report has these sections: where the time went; send-backs, each classified as a defect in the work, caused by the tooling or process, or a spec that was wrong; what the spec missed (amended or added criteria, tasks added mid-build, criteria reported as unsatisfiable, requirements without accepted evidence, reconcile gaps); staffing; cost; friction (stalls, flaky gate tests, operator waits); what worked; what to improve, each improvement labelled as about the project's code and checks, how its specs are written, how its builds are staffed and run, or the tooling itself; and the runs whose transcripts it read.

requirements.rationale: An ungrounded review finding cannot be checked or acted on; the Hub checking ids is how spec-vault-check already keeps a model honest.
requirements.statement: Every finding, lesson and improvement in a retrospective, whether from a part review or the final report, cites at least one task, run, event or evidence id belonging to that document's build; the Hub drops any that cites none or cites an id outside the build, and the report shows how many were dropped.

The document's spec page shows its newest retrospective with when it was made, what triggered it, the model, how many parts it was reviewed in and its cost; earlier retrospectives of the same document stay reachable; a failed firing shows as failed with the reason and a way to run it again.

requirements.rationale: Agents writing the next spec read the vault, not old spec pages; tracked so every machine working the project gets the same lessons (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: Each retrospective that is written adds one dated, tracked source to that project's vault holding its lessons, naming the document it reviewed, so the project's later turns on any machine find it through the vault map; it is queued for distillation when the distillation job is on.

A retrospective that is off, running, failed or empty never delays or refuses approving a task or approving or archiving a document; each firing, and each part of a firing, is recorded as a manager_job_fired event with its outcome and usage, like the other jobs.

requirements.rationale: Transcripts are needed to explain why a flagged event happened; unflagged transcripts are mostly file reads and test runs. The operator chose no budget on flagged transcripts (2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: A run's full transcript is included exactly when the run is flagged: it ended in a send-back, a stall names it, it failed or was stopped, it is a mender run, or its duration is more than twice the median of the build's runs. Every flagged run's transcript is included, with no budget, and the report lists the runs whose transcripts it read.

requirements.rationale: With no transcript budget, the builds most worth reviewing (long, troubled ones) are the ones that will not fit; a retrospective that fails on exactly those is worth little (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: When a build's input does not fit one call to the chosen model, the Hub splits it into parts that each fit, with no task's records divided across parts, reviews each part separately, and then writes one report from the part reviews and the build-wide figures; the report says how many parts it was reviewed in. A build that fits is reviewed in one call.

Each check run, whether a task's or a landing batch's, records the time it got a check slot, and the record survives a Hub restart. A run that never got a slot (cancelled or superseded while waiting) records none.

requirements.rationale: AWOAW's 2 h of check runs showed as 17 min because the wall bar gives overlapping instants to building first.
requirements.statement: A build's check figures count every check run for the build's tasks, including landing-batch runs, for its full duration, whether or not building or reviewing happened at the same time. The figures are: time running, time waiting for a slot, number of runs, number passed, number failed, and number timed out. A run in which any check ended by its time limit is counted as timed out and not as failed.

A check run with no recorded slot time counts its whole duration as running. When every run of a build lacks a slot time, the build's waiting figure is unknown (null), not zero. When only some runs lack one, the figure covers the runs that have one, and the build reports how many runs had no slot time.

A build's figures include, over its tasks that have landed on main, the total and the longest time from a task's last approval to its landing. They also give the number of approved tasks still waiting to land, and the longest wait among those so far.

The build card shows a Checks meter with check running time and slot-waiting time as its parts, and its total. Beside it, the card shows the timed-out count and the landing wait (total, longest, and any still waiting). The wall-time bar is unchanged. An unknown figure reads as unknown, not as 0.
